description: The study of Chemistry in Everyday Life under General Science deals with applied chemicals like polymers, drugs, glass, and cement. It helps in understanding important industrial and household compounds crucial for competitive exams.

sections.title: Polymers
sections.description: Study of macromolecules with high molecular mass formed by the combination of smaller units called monomers.

key_concepts.explanation: The chemical process in which small molecules called monomers join together to form a large molecule or polymer.
A natural polymer of isoprene, obtained from the latex of the rubber tree.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The process of heating natural rubber with sulfur.
scientific_principles.application: Makes rubber stronger, harder, and more elastic, which is essential for manufacturing vehicle tires.

key_associations.extra_info: Used extensively in packaging and making carry bags.
Used as a non-stick coating on cookware.
Used for manufacturing water pipes and electrical cable insulation.
A thermosetting plastic used for making electrical switches and handles of cooking utensils.

important_facts.fact: Nylon-6,6 was the first fully synthetic fiber created by humans.

sections.title: Drugs and Medicines
sections.description: Classification of chemical substances used for the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases.

key_concepts.explanation: Medicines used to lower the body temperature during a high fever.
Chemical substances produced by microorganisms that inhibit the growth of or destroy other harmful microorganisms.
Alkaline substances that neutralize excess stomach acid to relieve heartburn and indigestion.

historical_events.significance: Discovered by Alexander Fleming, it was the first antibiotic and revolutionized modern medical science.

key_associations.extra_info: Commonly used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain.
Extracted from the bark of the Cinchona tree.

important_facts.fact: The chemical name of Aspirin is Acetylsalicylic Acid; it is also used to prevent heart attacks due to its blood-thinning (anti-clotting) properties.

sections.title: Glass
sections.description: Glass is a transparent, amorphous, and supercooled liquid lacking a crystalline structure.

key_concepts.explanation: Glass is not a true solid; it is a liquid that has been cooled to a rigid state without undergoing crystallization.
The process of slowly cooling hot glass to relieve internal stresses and prevent it from cracking.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Specific colors are imparted to glass by adding transition metal oxides to the molten mixture.
scientific_principles.application: Cobalt Oxide gives a deep blue color, while Chromium Oxide gives a green color.

key_associations.extra_info: A type of borosilicate glass that is highly resistant to heat and thermal shock.
Has a high refractive index, making it ideal for optical instruments.
Specially designed to absorb harmful Ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun.

important_facts.fact: Glass is highly soluble in Hydrofluoric Acid (HF), which is why this acid is never stored in glass bottles.

sections.title: Cement
sections.description: A major binding material used in construction, primarily consisting of a mixture of calcium silicates and aluminates.

key_concepts.explanation: The most common type of cement, named so because its hardened state resembles Portland stone quarried in England.
Small, solid nodules formed by heating limestone and clay at high temperatures, which are then ground to make cement.

historical_events.significance: Invented and patented by English bricklayer Joseph Aspdin.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: An exothermic reaction involving the hydration of cement particles when mixed with water.
scientific_principles.application: Provides structural strength and rigidity to walls, roofs, and dams.

key_associations.extra_info: Excess lime causes cement to crack upon setting, while a deficiency makes the cement weak.
Added (2-3%) during grinding to prevent the cement from setting too quickly (flash setting).

important_facts.fact: In RCC (Reinforced Concrete Cement), iron or steel rods are embedded within the concrete to massively increase its tensile strength.

sections.title: Soaps and Detergents
sections.description: Surface-active agents (surfactants) primarily used for washing and cleansing purposes.

key_concepts.explanation: The chemical process of making soap by heating vegetable oils or animal fats with a strong alkali like Caustic Soda (NaOH) or Caustic Potash (KOH).
A spherical cluster of soap molecules in water that traps dirt or oil at its center, allowing it to be washed away.

key_associations.extra_info: Generally used for washing clothes and general cleaning.
Gentler on the skin, used for bathing soaps, liquid soaps, and shaving creams.

important_facts.fact: Soap does not form lather well in hard water, whereas synthetic detergents work effectively in both hard and soft water.
Glycerol (Glycerin) is produced as a valuable by-product during the saponification process.
